The short tour with me through the most important features.
Here I explain how to find your TV and connect it to me.

Elly works with LG TVs running webOS.
• Android 9 or newer on your phone.
• Phone and TV on the same network (Wi-Fi or a network cable on the TV).
• The TV must be switched on when you connect it for the first time.

On first start, the settings open on the “TV” tab after the quick start, and Elly immediately looks for LG TVs on the local network. Found TVs are listed with name, model and IP address.\nThe search takes a few seconds. “Search again” starts it once more.

If the search doesn\'t find your TV, enter its address under “Enter IP address” (e.g. 192.168.0.10) and tap “Connect”.\nYou\'ll find the IP address in the network settings of the TV or in the device list of your router.

Select a TV. A connection request appears on the TV – accept it with the TV\'s own remote. After that Elly remembers the TV, so this is only needed once.\nWhile pairing, Elly also remembers the network address (MAC) of the TV to be able to switch it on later.

You can pair several TVs. The “TV” tab of the settings lists them under “Paired TVs”; tap one to make it the active TV. “Remove” deletes a TV together with its screen layout after asking.\nYou can open the “TV” tab any time by tapping the TV name in the top bar.

If the TV is off, the power key sends a wake-up signal over the network (Wake-on-LAN). For this to work, the option “Turn on via Wi-Fi” (on some models “Mobile TV On”) must be enabled on the TV.\nSwitching off always works as long as the TV is connected.

• Not reachable: check that the TV is switched on and on the same network. On some models “LG Connect Apps” must be enabled in the network settings.
• Rejected: the request was declined on the TV. Select the TV again and accept the request.
• Timeout: the TV didn't answer in time. Please try again.
• Certificate changed: after a software update of the TV its security certificate can change. Remove the TV and pair it again.

The demo mode (Settings → tab “TV”) simulates a connected TV. All screens can be used, no commands are sent. The status light is yellow and the top bar shows “Demo TV”.\nThe demo mode has its own screen layout. Switch it off to control your TV again.
This is how the remote is organised: top bar, screens and how the keys react.

The top bar is visible on every screen:
• TV name with status light: opens the settings on the “TV” tab.
• Pointer key (mouse symbol): opens the pointer. While it is active, the symbol is blue.
• Gear: opens the settings of Elly.
• Elly at the far right: opens this help.

• Green: connected.
• Red: TV not reachable.
• Grey: checking the connection.
• Yellow: demo mode.
While Elly is visible, the connection is checked every 10 seconds and after every key press. When the app goes to the background, the connection is closed.

The keys are spread across up to four screens, so everything fits without scrolling. Swipe left or right to switch. The dots at the bottom show which screen you are on; with only one active screen they disappear.\nElly remembers the screen you used last. Which screens are shown and in which order is set in the settings.

• Keys trigger when you lift your finger. A swipe that starts on a key therefore sends nothing.
• Volume, channel and the direction pad repeat while you hold them.
• If you like, the phone vibrates on every key press (Settings → “Controls”).
• If a key isn't available or the TV can't be reached, a message appears at the bottom.

• Screen 1: power, screen off/on, TV settings, guide, home, direction pad, volume and channel rockers, mute, live TV, back and color keys.
• Screen 2: number keys, guide, •••, mute, live TV, rockers, direction pad, back, input and color keys.
• Screen 3: record, stop, rewind, pause, play, fast forward, direction pad, back, color keys and app keys (Netflix, Prime Video, Rakuten TV).
• Screen 4: empty and hidden, for your own layout.
You can rearrange every screen freely and reset it at any time.

When a text field is active on the TV (e.g. a search), a text bar opens automatically at the bottom. What you type is sent to the TV live; the send key works like Enter.\nWith the “Keyboard” key (can be added in the editor) you open the text bar by hand. Apps with their own on-screen keyboard sometimes don\'t accept the text.
Here you\'ll find every key and what it does on the TV.
Switches the TV off. If it can\'t be reached, Elly sends a wake-up signal (see “Switching the TV on”).
Switches only the TV screen off or back on, the sound keeps playing – handy for music or audio books.
• Volume rocker: louder / quieter.\n• Mute: sound off / on.\n• Channel rocker (CH): channel up / down.
Direction pad, OK, back and home
• Direction pad: navigate through menus, OK in the middle confirms.\n• Back: one step back.\n• Home: webOS home screen.
TV settings, guide, live TV and •••

• Gear on the screen: settings of the TV (not of Elly).
• Guide (GUIDE): the TV program guide.
• Live TV (TV with antenna): switches to TV reception via antenna, cable or satellite.
• •••: opens the “More actions” menu of the TV.
Opens a list of the inputs the TV reports (e.g. HDMI 1, HDMI 2) and switches to the one you choose. Inputs without a connected device are marked “Nothing connected”.
Rewind, pause, play, fast forward and stop control the current playback. Record starts a recording if the TV supports it. How well the keys work depends on the app on the TV.
Red, green, yellow and blue – e.g. for teletext or for functions an app on the TV offers.
An app key opens an app on the TV, e.g. Netflix. It shows the app icon from the TV and/or a text. How to set up app keys is described under “Setting up app keys”.
With the pointer you click your way through the TV – by moving your phone or with the touchpad.

The pointer key in the top bar opens the pointer – just like with the Magic Remote, a cursor appears on the TV. In both modes:
• OK clicks at the pointer position, several clicks in a row are possible.
• The X at the top right or the back gesture closes the pointer, the cursor on the TV disappears.
• After 5 seconds without activity the pointer closes automatically.
Whether you steer with motion or the touchpad is chosen in the settings (gear in the top bar) on the “Controls” tab. All other options in this chapter are there too.

The pointer follows the movements of your phone. Two ways of holding it are recognised automatically:
• Like a remote (screen facing up, top edge pointing to the TV): swing left/right, tilt the top edge up/down.
• Upright in front of you (back facing the TV): turn left/right, tilt forward/back.
Twisting around the pointing direction is ignored so the cursor stays steady. Swipe up or down on the scroll area to scroll. Motion mode needs a gyroscope in the phone.

• Sensitivity (0.3× to 3.0×): how far the pointer moves per movement.\n• Acceleration (0× to 4×): fast swings move the pointer disproportionately far, slow ones stay precise. 0 switches acceleration off.
The pointer follows your finger like on a laptop touchpad. A short tap without swiping clicks. “Speed” (0.3× to 3.0×) sets how far the pointer moves per swipe.

Like an analog stick: the further you drag in a direction, the faster the pointer moves.
• Free position: the stick starts where you first touch the area.
• Fixed: the stick is always visible in the middle; a short tap clicks.
The inner circle is the dead zone: as long as the knob stays inside, the pointer doesn't move.
OK button at the top or bottom
In touchpad mode the OK button sits at the bottom (default) or at the top – whichever suits the way you hold your phone.

• Open by shaking (motion mode): a short shake of the phone opens the pointer. The shake sensitivity can be adjusted.\n• Open by double tap (touchpad mode): tap twice on a free spot of a screen.\nBoth are enabled in the settings under “Controls”.
You decide which keys go where. Here I show you the editor.

Under Settings → “Appearance” → “Screens” you see previews of your four screens.
• Tap to show or hide a screen. At least one stays active.
• Hold and drag to change the order.
• The pen opens the editor, the arrow resets the screen after asking.
Everything is saved per TV.

The editor shows the screen as a grid (24 × 48 cells) in the proportions of the real screen. Elements always cover whole cells. Keys become round if their area is nearly square, otherwise oblong.\n“Done” saves and closes the editor.

“+ Element” opens a selection with two tabs:
• Keys: every single key, volume and channel rocker, direction pad and app key.
• Key groups: e.g. number keys, video controls, color keys or volume + channel. Groups are inserted as single keys.
New elements go to the first free spot, made a little smaller if necessary.
• Drag to move an element.\n• Tap to select it; the handle at the corner changes its size.\n• Drag it onto the bin to remove it.
Drag a frame on a free area to select several elements. Move the selection together or drag it onto the bin together.

Undo takes back the last steps (up to 50): adding, moving, resizing, removing, app keys and resetting. The history starts anew each time you open the editor.\nReset restores the default layout of the screen after asking.

Hold an app key in the editor for 2 seconds. The “App key” window opens with a preview:
• Choose app: loads the apps from the TV and assigns one. The icon is saved on the phone and visible even without a connection.
• Appearance: icon and/or text, your own text and text color. The text shrinks automatically to fit the key.
Changes only apply with OK. If an icon is missing, Elly loads it as soon as the TV is connected.
Make me pretty! Colors, background and shapes are set in the settings.
Tap the gear in the top bar and choose the “Appearance” tab in the settings. Everything in this chapter is there. Changes apply to all screens right away.

15 palettes color keys, rockers, direction pad and app keys: Graphite, Silver, Ocean, Forest, Copper, Violet, Petrol, Bordeaux, Sand, Coral, Midnight, Sage, Ruby, Lagoon and Amber. Power and the color keys keep their colors.

The background applies to all screens:
• None: plain dark.
• Auto: matching the color palette.
• Own image: from your photo picker, scaled proportionally and cropped.
• Motifs: hills, ocean, meadow, sky, aurora, graphite, mountains, forest and sea.
Two sliders set how round the corners are: “Keys” applies to keys, rockers and app keys, “Direction pad” to the ring and the OK key. The preview shows the result right away.
A light effect: low light from the top left, the keys cast long, soft shadows to the bottom right and the background brightens from that corner. Available from Android 12.
With the widgets you control your TV straight from the home screen.

• Elly volume: louder / quieter.
• Elly channel: channel up / down.
• Elly playback: rewind, play, pause, fast forward, stop.
• Elly power.
• Elly mute.
• Elly screen: screen off / on.
• Elly remote: all of these keys in one widget. In its widget settings you choose which keys it shows; the layout rearranges itself.
Add them like any other widget: long-press a free spot on the home screen and choose “Widgets”.
When you add a widget, Elly asks which TV it should control. You can change this later in the widget settings (hold the widget).

• The app doesn't need to be open.
• With vibration enabled (settings, “Controls” tab), the widget vibrates too.
• If the TV can't be reached, a message appears.
• From Android 12 the widgets take on the colors of your wallpaper.
Let\'s tinker with the settings. I\'ll show you where to find what.

The gear in the top bar opens the settings. They have three tabs, which you can also swipe between; Elly remembers the one you opened last.
• TV: paired TVs, search, IP address, demo mode.
• Appearance: screens, color palette, background, rounding, light effect.
• Controls: pointer and vibration.

The “TV” tab lists your paired TVs at the top: tap one to make it active. “Remove” unpairs it after asking; to use the TV again you have to pair it again.\nBelow, you can search for more TVs or enter an IP address.\nWhile demo mode is on, the tab only shows its switch; turn it off to pair or switch TVs.
A short vibration on every key press, also when clicking in touchpad mode and on the widgets.
Your data belongs to you. That is my verdict, and it is final!
Elly only talks to your TV on the local network, no data is sent to external servers. Paired TVs, settings, screen layouts and app icons stay on your phone and are deleted when you uninstall the app.
The full privacy policy is opened via “Privacy” at the bottom of the settings, next to the version number.
